args.summary: The latest production deploy of checkout-api (v2.3.1) began failing health checks across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. In response, the service was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (note: v2.3.1-rc was healthy in staging only). Rollback completed and verified: all regions now running v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate back down to ~0.2%. Note: v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so any redeploy will require change-manager approval.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Summary of actions:

1. **Diagnosed**: The latest deploy of checkout-api, **v2.3.1**, was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an ~18% error rate.
2. **Rolled back** all production regions to **v2.3.0** — the most recent release that was healthy *in production*. (v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging, so it was not eligible.)
3. **Verified recovery**: all regions now run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate dropped to ~0.2%.
4. **Opened SEV2 incident INC-0001** documenting the failure and the rollback; the on-call engineer has been paged. The incident also notes that v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so redeploying it will require change-manager approval per policy.
